challenger_of: CROSS_SECTIONAL_MOMENTUM_LIVE_V1 (reports/live_alpha_lab/CROSS_SECTIONAL_MOMENTUM_LIVE_V1/freeze_spec.json, freeze_timestamp=2026-08-31T18:30:44+00:00 -- STRICTLY EARLIER, untouched by this build) -- V2 is a PARALLEL challenger, not a replacement: both alpha_ids, both ledgers, both track records exist independently and permanently.
mechanism: Cross-sectional 7-day trailing return momentum, long-only, top-quintile weekly selection -- IDENTICAL causal math to V1 -- within a DYNAMIC, PIT-resolved liquid-altcoin universe (not V1's fixed frozen-50). See CROSS_SECTIONAL_MOMENTUM_PIT_V1 (configs/live_alpha_registry.yaml, still DATA_BLOCKED, untouched) for the true original spec (PIT 312-symbol universe, data_v2/normalized).
source_report: reports/edge_discovery/alpha_hunt_2026-08-30/w1_cross_sectional/REPORT.md rank 1 (M1), 'Detail on the two most promising candidates' section 1, robustness-checks paragraph
reconstruction_rationale: V1 (built earlier the same day) is a lightweight live reconstruction that deliberately kept the ORIGINAL frozen-50-symbol universe (configs/portfolio_v1_1_parallel_50.yaml, majors/large-established-alt biased). V1's own freeze_spec.json flags an important honest caveat: the source report's own robustness checks found the effect is an 'altcoin breadth' phenomenon -- it works in the 'mid/liquid' liquidity terciles but NOT in the illiquid tercile (t=0.19), and 'majors-only' alone is INSIGNIFICANT (t=0.72). V1's frozen-50 universe sits closer to 'majors' than to the broad liquid cross-section the source actually measured, so V1 may be testing a materially weaker (or absent) version of the effect. V2 exists specifically to test the mechanism on a universe that is actually broad and altcoin-heavy, per explicit user instruction: 'creer seulement comme CHALLENGER : CROSS_SECTIONAL_MOMENTUM_LIVE_V2 avec univers PIT dynamique de liquid alts, si ce chemin peut etre construit causalement' -- while staying live-data-only and NOT falling back on the DATA_BLOCKED data_v2/instrument_master.parquet panel (which only exists in the separate futur-data-v2 worktree, no confirmed continuous live update).

data_investigation.instrument_universe_source: Binance USDM futures public REST /fapi/v1/exchangeInfo (https://fapi.binance.com/fapi/v1/exchangeInfo) -- the SAME live endpoint symbol_resolver.py already uses for V1's listing-eligibility check, reused READ-ONLY here (fetch_exchange_info()) as the PRIMARY universe source instead of a secondary eligibility check on top of a fixed list. Queried fresh every run, no caching of exchangeInfo itself (negligible network cost, same design choice symbol_resolver.py already makes).
data_investigation.candidate_filter: contractType=PERPETUAL AND quoteAsset=USDT AND status=TRADING AND underlyingType=COIN AND symbol.isascii() -- see src/institutional/engines/cross_sectional_momentum_live_v2/universe.py docstring for the full field-by-field rationale, in particular the underlyingType=COIN filter: exchangeInfo at build time (2026-09-01) ALSO returns tokenized EQUITY/CN_EQUITY/HK_EQUITY/KR_EQUITY/COMMODITY/PREMARKET underlyings and basket/INDEX products (e.g. BTCDOMUSDT, a BTC-dominance index) on the exact same endpoint -- all excluded, not swept in by an unqualified 'all USDT perpetuals' filter. The isascii() clause was added AFTER the actual first run below hit it in practice (see known_risks/notes) -- 4 candidates carry non-ASCII (CJK) vanity ticker names that crash the shared (V1, frozen, not modified here) klines REST client's URL construction; excluded explicitly and deterministically rather than relying on that client's caught-exception fallback.
data_investigation.candidate_count_verified_at_build: 523 symbols passed the first four criteria when queried live on 2026-09-01 (verified by direct API call during this build, not assumed) -- vs 128 symbols in status=SETTLING (correctly excluded) and 2 INDEX-underlying USDT perpetuals (BTCDOMUSDT, ALLUSDT, correctly excluded). Of those 523, 4 carried non-ASCII ticker names (see candidate_filter note) and are excluded by the isascii() clause -- 519 final candidates. Roughly ~10x V1's 49-symbol eligible universe.
data_investigation.price_volume_source: Same as V1: Binance USDM futures public REST /fapi/v1/klines (interval=1d), no API key. klines_source.py (src/institutional/engines/cross_sectional_momentum_live/klines_source.py) reused READ-ONLY -- it is a generic Binance daily-klines REST client + local parquet cache with zero alpha-specific business logic baked in (takes exchange_symbol + cache_path as plain arguments), so reusing it here is not a modification of V1 and does not duplicate ~170 lines of network/retry code. V2's OWN code (the actual points of behavioral difference from V1) lives entirely in universe.py (candidate resolution) and signal.py (V2's own MIN_LIQUIDITY_USD, see below) plus the runner script and this freeze_spec/registry entry.
data_investigation.data_v2_instrument_master: The ORIGINAL spec's universe source (312-symbol PIT panel). DATA_BLOCKED per CROSS_SECTIONAL_MOMENTUM_PIT_V1 -- lives only in the separate futur-data-v2 worktree, no continuous live update confirmed. Not used here, same as V1.

universe.type: DYNAMIC (PIT) -- re-resolved from live exchangeInfo on every run, NOT a fixed list. This is the core mechanism difference from V1.
universe.candidate_resolution: src/institutional/engines/cross_sectional_momentum_live_v2/universe.py::resolve_dynamic_liquid_universe(exchange_info) -- pure filter over a live exchangeInfo response, no caching, no fail-closed hash-drift gate (a changing set of TRADING symbols run-to-run is expected and correct here, unlike V1's frozen-hash guard which exists precisely because V1's universe must NOT drift). Every run writes its resolved candidate set to reports/live_alpha_lab/CROSS_SECTIONAL_MOMENTUM_LIVE_V2/_universe_resolution.json for audit -- nothing silent even though nothing is gated.
universe.liquidity_filter: Same causal mechanism as V1 (trailing 30-day MEDIAN daily quote-asset-volume, USD, via signal.py::trailing_liquidity_usd) but a DIFFERENT threshold: min_liquidity_usd=$2,000,000 (2x V1's $1,000,000 verbatim-source floor). See threshold_provenance below for the full justification -- this is the one number in this spec that is a genuine, documented engineering judgment call rather than a verbatim source constant.
universe.threshold_provenance: The source report applies a base '>=$1M trailing-30d median daily quote-volume' liquid-cohort filter over its FULL 312-symbol candidate universe (VERBATIM number, same as V1 uses), then reports that WITHIN that liquid cohort, the effect works in the 'mid' and 'liquid' liquidity TERCILES but NOT in the 'illiquid' tercile (t=0.19) -- i.e. even among names clearing the $1M floor, a further liquidity split matters, and the report does not publish the numeric tercile boundaries (same 'constant not published' situation this registry already documents for several RECONSTRUCTED entries). V2's raw candidate universe (523 symbols, all currently-TRADING USDT perpetuals) is far larger and far younger on average than the source's 312-symbol PIT panel -- it includes many very recently listed 2026-vintage micro-cap/meme perpetuals (verified present at build time: symbols with prefixes like '1000000BOB', '1000000MOG', short tickers like '4USDT'/'2ZUSDT') that a human-curated fixed list would never include and that plausibly sit disproportionately in the source's 'illiquid tercile' bucket. Reusing the verbatim $1M floor here, without the tercile split the source found necessary, risked materially over-including exactly the cohort the source found does NOT work. Absent the published tercile boundaries, min_liquidity_usd was set to $2,000,000 as a documented, CONSERVATIVE proxy for 'closer to mid/liquid, further from illiquid' -- NOT a value read off any historical panel, NOT grid-searched against this alpha's own historical returns (no data-snooping against the observations this alpha will be judged on). This is an honest approximation, not a reproduction, of the source's tercile split -- flagged explicitly as a real source of uncertainty in the notes below and in the registry entry.
universe.deviation_from_v1: V1 keeps the ORIGINAL curated frozen-50 list (majors + large established alts) with live listing-eligibility resolved on top. V2 replaces that fixed list entirely with the dynamic candidate-then-liquidity-filter pipeline above. V1's frozen-50 is, at build time, very close to a subset of V2's much larger eligible universe -- the two are NOT independent bets on different assets, they are the SAME mechanism applied to overlapping-but-different universes (see correlation_family note in the registry entry).
universe.deviation_from_pit_v1: Same high-level deviation V1 already documents (live REST klines instead of the data_v2/normalized PIT panel; a universe resolved from CURRENT exchange metadata instead of the true historical-PIT 312-symbol panel) -- V2 additionally deviates in NOT being restricted to a small hand-picked list, which is what makes it a genuine attempt at the source's own 'broad liquid altcoin' framing rather than a majors-biased subset. Still not a byte-for-byte reproduction: no historical exchangeInfo snapshot exists, so today's TRADING status is used as a (mild) proxy for historical PIT listing eligibility -- see known_risks below.
universe.survivorship_caveat: Binance does not expose a historical listing-status feed -- only TODAY's exchangeInfo TRADING flag is known. A symbol delisted before this alpha's build date never appears anywhere in the backfilled history, even for the (historical) weeks it was actually trading and liquid. This is the same limitation V1 already carries (documented in V1's own freeze_spec.json) -- not new to V2, but proportionally larger here because V2's candidate set is much bigger and includes many more names with a real chance of eventual delisting than V1's curated majors-heavy list.

frozen_spec.rebalance_weekday: Monday (pd.Timestamp.weekday()==0) -- same fixed anchor as V1, unchanged.
frozen_spec.direction: LONG only, hard-enforced in the runner (RuntimeError if any non-LONG row ever appears) -- SHORT_REJECTED (standing project rule), same as V1.
frozen_spec.signal: tret_7d = close[t]/close[t-7]-1, causal, computed on daily USDM futures close prices from live REST klines, reindexed to a gap-free daily calendar before the shift (so lookback=7 rows == 7 calendar days). Identical formula to V1.
frozen_spec.liquidity_filter: trailing 30-day MEDIAN daily quote-asset-volume (USD) >= $2,000,000 -- V2's OWN threshold, see universe.threshold_provenance above. NOT verbatim from the source report (which specifies $1M as its base filter, then an unpublished tercile split).
frozen_spec.selection: top ceil(0.20 * n_eligible) symbols by tret_7d among the liquidity-eligible cohort at each Monday rebalance. top_fraction=0.20 (quintile) unchanged from V1 and from the source report's own verbatim-recommended bucket.
frozen_spec.current_day_handling: the in-progress UTC daily bar (today, not yet closed) is dropped from the panel before any computation, same as V1.

expected_stats_at_freeze.note: HISTORICAL CONTEXT ONLY from the source report's PIT 312-symbol full-sample measurement (SAME figures V1's freeze_spec.json cites) -- NOT a forward target for this reconstruction, which uses a different (larger, dynamically-resolved, higher-liquidity-floor) universe and a different (live REST) data source than what produced these numbers. Do not read forward edge_retention against these figures without re-deriving a universe-appropriate baseline.
expected_stats_at_freeze.cost_model_note: Same caveat as V1: the source's 20bps is a market-neutral LONG-SHORT quintile-spread floor (4 legs, 100% turnover). NOT directly applicable to this long-only reconstruction. No net_bps target is claimed for V2's actual universe/costs -- Mode A here is signal-only, no fills simulated, no cost applied to any row.

api_load_accounting.first_run_call_estimate: up to ~523-1000 GET /fapi/v1/klines calls (1-2 pages/symbol depending on listing age -- majors listed since ~2019-2020 need 2 pages at limit=1500/1d bars back to 2020-01-01, most 2026-vintage listings need only 1)
api_load_accounting.weight_per_call: 10 (limit=1500 klines call, per Binance's published USDM futures weight table)
api_load_accounting.public_rate_limit_assumption: ~2400 request-weight/minute/IP (Binance public USDM futures REST, standard documented tier at build time)
api_load_accounting.pacing: klines_source.py already sleeps 0.15s between pages within one symbol (pre-existing, unmodified); the V2 runner additionally sleeps INTER_SYMBOL_SLEEP_SEC=0.12s between symbols. Combined with real network round-trip latency, this naturally paces a full ~523-symbol backfill well under the per-minute weight budget rather than bursting all calls at once -- verified in practice by the actual first run (see run_state.json for wall-clock duration and _universe_resolution.json for the exact candidate list used).
api_load_accounting.steady_state_cost: every run after the first is incremental per symbol (refresh_symbol_cache only fetches from the last cached date forward) -- typically 0-1 new daily bar/symbol/day, i.e. cheap, no different in kind from V1's steady-state cost.
api_load_accounting.no_new_infrastructure: No new persistent collector/daemon/systemd service was started for this alpha -- all REST polling happens on-demand inside the runner script, same as V1, per the mission's explicit instruction.

correlated_with: CROSS_SECTIONAL_MOMENTUM_LIVE_V1 (SAME correlation_family, SAME economic mechanism, SUBSTANTIALLY OVERLAPPING universe -- V1's frozen-50 sits close to a subset of V2's ~523-symbol candidate set. These are correlated bets, not independent ones; the portfolio dedup layer's max_dominant_per_correlation_family logic should treat CROSS_SECTIONAL_MOMENTUM_LIVE_V1 and _V2 as the same cluster, never sized as if independent.)

CROSS_SECTIONAL_MOMENTUM_PIT_V1 (DATA_BLOCKED, same economic family/correlation_family, true original spec -- not the same universe/data as either live variant, do not treat as independently corroborating).

CROSS_SECTIONAL_LONG (src/institutional/engines/cross_sectional_long/infer.py, existing heuristic AlphaEngine on data/enriched 8-symbol universe -- a different construction (momentum_score heuristic, not raw tret_7d), not this alpha, do not confuse in reporting).
execution_notes: No simulated fills. Mode B (execution shadow) not implemented for this alpha.
known_risks: 4/523 raw candidates (0.8%) carry non-ASCII vanity ticker names and are excluded upfront by universe.py's isascii() filter (added after the actual first run hit V1's shared klines client's UnicodeEncodeError on them) -- economically negligible (novelty listings, would very likely have failed the $2M liquidity floor regardless) but documented here for completeness per this repo's bug-disclosure discipline. Not fixed inside klines_source.py itself because that file belongs to V1 (frozen, off-limits per the mission) -- fixed instead as an explicit V2-only exclusion criterion.

Universe-threshold judgment call: $2M liquidity floor is a documented engineering choice, not a verbatim source number or a reproduction of the source's unpublished liquidity-tercile split -- see universe.threshold_provenance. The true 'mid/liquid tercile' the source found significant could in principle be narrower or wider than what this floor selects.

Broader universe = more noise per the mission's own caution: many more names competing for the same top-quintile slice each week means more idiosyncratic single-name risk per selected name, not necessarily more edge -- this is an open empirical question this forward track record is meant to answer, not assumed away.

Thinner liquidity per name than V1's majors-heavy frozen-50, even after the $2M floor -- a materially higher execution-cost reality if this were ever promoted past Mode A (not relevant to Mode A itself, which simulates no fills, but relevant to any future promotion decision).

Mild survivorship bias in the backfilled/replay history, since only symbols TRADING today are ever considered (see universe.survivorship_caveat above) -- inherited from V1's same limitation, proportionally larger given V2's much bigger raw candidate set.
Correlated with V1 by construction (same mechanism, overlapping universe) -- see correlated_with above; must not be portfolio-sized as an independent sleeve.
do_not_modify_after_this_timestamp: Any change to entry/threshold/universe-filter/data source after freeze_timestamp must be a new alpha_id (e.g. _V3), not an edit to this spec.
